plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid regardless of how high I bid above my value, and bidding above my value only risks winning when I'd have negative profit. Bidding below my value only risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal bid equals my private value of $9.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($9), I win only when my value exceeds both competitors' bids, and I pay the second-highest bid, guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to adjust from, truthful bidding remains optimal.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding exactly my value ensures that if I win, I pay the second-highest bid which is always less than my value, guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks negative profit if I win at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily. With no history to adjust for, truthful bidding is optimal.
